title: Percentages and Discounts: Percentages of Amounts, GST and Sales

key_sub: With a calculator, multiply by the decimal: 17% of 340 = 0.17 × 340. To add GST of 10%, multiply by 1.1.
body_html:
How it works

Without a calculator, build from easy percentages: 10% = ÷ 10, 5% = half of 10%, 1% = ÷ 100, 50% = half, 25% = a quarter.

With a calculator, use a multiplier: 17% of 340 = 0.17 × 340. To increase by 20%, multiply by 1.2; to decrease by 20%, multiply by 0.8.

To write one amount as a percentage of another: divide, then × 100.

Example

Find 35% of 240.

10% = 24, so 30% = 72.

5% = 12.

35% = 72 + 12.

Answer: 84

Example

Decrease $80 by 15%.

15% of $80 = $12.

$80 − $12 = $68. (Or 0.85 × 80.)

Answer: $68

Example

What is 18 out of 30 as a percentage?

18/30 = 0.6.

0.6 × 100 = 60%.

Answer: 60%

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the percentage: 20% of 80 is 16, not 80 ÷ 20 = 4.
  • Stopping at the change: a 25% discount on $80 makes the price $60, not $20.
  • Using 0.5 for 5%: 5% as a decimal is 0.05.
  • Dividing the wrong way round: 18 out of 30 is 18 ÷ 30, not 30 ÷ 18.

faq.a: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100. 18 out of 30 = 18 ÷ 30 × 100 = 60%.
